name: Patch: ABORT backlog and fidelity fixes
summary:
Ship 0.4.1: a patch release closing the open items the v0.4.0 ABORT review recorded, and two of the five fidelity problems it accepted. Continuous integration now runs the gates that were hand-run — it found a Linux-only defect on its first run — and the vendored bundles carry verified digests. Asset loading is bounded by file type as well as directory, so files beside a document are no longer readable on render; saving refuses to clobber a change made on disk, preserves extended attributes and refuses a read-only target; and a bounded event trail with build identity means a reported failure can be root-caused. Inline
is no longer deleted and CRLF line endings survive an edit. The accepted GA blocker remains open and is now scoped from measurement rather than from review findings: it is five problems, not one, and inline HTML was never the cause. See docs/decisions/2026-08-08-markdown-fidelity-scope.md.

required.title: Current editor screen functional sweep
required.summary: Visible enabled controls on the current formatted/empty shell are backed or removed; formatting commands operate on selected/current block content.

required.title: Raw screen backed slice
required.summary: Raw mode has source-editor layout, Syntax Legend side panel, backed soft-wrap and line-number toggles, and markdown round-trip preservation.

required.title: Split screen and Insert popover
required.summary: Split mode has a real source pane, derived formatted preview, mode round-trip preservation, and a backed Insert popover command path.

required.title: Settings backed slice
required.summary: Settings opens from persistent title-bar chrome, stays out of document-view ribbon context, stages runtime preference drafts, loads installed font options from the native app, applies backed document/code typography and raw-editor preferences on Save, and discards drafts on Cancel.

required.title: Source and fenced-code syntax highlighting
required.summary: Raw and Split source modes render markdown syntax highlighting through a synchronized overlay, and fenced code blocks highlight using their declared backtick language.

required.title: Code Block language assistant
required.summary: Formatted-mode Code Block controls open a language chooser and insert fenced code blocks with the selected language info string.

required.title: Mermaid Diagram assistant
required.summary: Visible Mermaid Diagram insert controls open a type-specific assistant with editable fields and live Mermaid rendering; Mermaid fenced blocks render as diagrams in formatted and split preview modes.

required.title: Chrome density pass
required.summary: Removed the duplicated in-canvas title bar and moved Settings into the ribbon tab row as an application-level control.

required.title: Ribbon icon system and save-dialog alert cleanup
required.summary: Insert ribbon actions use local SVG symbols instead of hand-drawn CSS glyphs, and Wails message dialogs use a transparent icon override to remove redundant alert artwork.

required.title: Independent side-panel visibility
required.summary: The file rail and document outline/raw-assistance panel can be hidden and restored independently without changing markdown or editor mode.

required.title: Rendered markdown fidelity
required.summary: Align formatted and split-preview rendering with the design package: document typography, inline markdown semantics, code block chrome, and Mermaid theming.

required.title: Split mode parity
required.summary: Split mode has constrained equal panes, explicit scroll-lock labeling, and proportional two-way scroll synchronization.

required.title: Ribbon completion and command taxonomy
required.summary: Home and Insert expose backed Image and Math insertion, Help opens backed help panels, Export opens a backed Print/PDF menu, and Share remains hidden until collaboration exists.

required.title: Settings completion
required.summary: Settings exposes backed Editor and Appearance controls, moves into the primary tab row, applies runtime preferences, and marks future Markdown, Sync, and Extensions sections disabled until native behavior exists.

required.title: Side panels and empty state polish
required.summary: The empty state no longer repeats app chrome or document title copy, suppresses the document inspector until content exists, and collapsed side panels expose compact labelled restore rails.

required.title: Contextual document controls
required.summary: Table, Code Block, and Mermaid Diagram controls now appear on the document surface when matching blocks exist, reusing backed markdown transforms for in-place management.

required.title: Accessibility and native feel pass
required.summary: Transient surfaces now support Escape dismissal, dialogs focus their first actionable control, and mode controls expose synchronized aria-pressed state.

required.title: Print and PDF export
required.summary: Print and Export to PDF now render the active markdown into a formatted print document and invoke the macOS print dialog path, keeping application chrome out of printed output.

required.title: Visual regression baseline
required.summary: E2E screenshot coverage now exercises empty, formatted, raw, split, and settings surfaces at a constrained desktop width, guarding against blank renders and ribbon overflow.

required.title: Code block language context access
required.summary: Existing non-Mermaid code blocks can open the Code Block Language dialog from either right-click or a hover language tool, targeting the acted-on fenced block.

required.title: Native state, preferences, and recents foundation
required.summary: The Wails app API now uses injected native/document/font/preference ports, backed settings persist through a local JSON preference store, recent documents are recorded after open/save, and the start screen can reopen recent files through a specific bridge method.

required.title: Responsive shell adaptation
required.summary: Reduced-width desktop windows now compact labelled ribbon controls to icon-sized controls with accessible labels/tooltips, wrap the ribbon instead of clipping, and collapse side panels at narrow widths to preserve the document canvas.

required.title: Editable source token layer
required.summary: Raw and Split source modes now render tokenized markdown marker spans and expose a backed Hide markers option that hides marker glyphs without changing textarea source content.

required.title: Cursor-precise document block model
required.summary: Contextual table controls now target the selected rendered table, existing Mermaid Diagrams can be selected and replaced independently, and existing code-block language targeting remains intact.

required.title: Obfuscated link schemes no longer reach the Go bindings
required.summary: The link allowlist checked the raw destination while the browser navigates a normalized one. The URL parser strips every ASCII tab, LF and CR and ignores leading control characters before parsing a scheme, so `jav<TAB>ascript:` carried no scheme by the check's reading and `javascript:` by the parser's — and a javascript: URL runs in the app origin, where the bindings expose SaveDocument and OpenRecentDocument with no path restriction, giving a document arbitrary file read and write. The check now normalizes exactly what the parser normalizes, resolves every candidate against a base so there is no looks-relative branch to slip past, and returns the href to assign rather than a boolean so a caller cannot validate one string and use another.

required.title: Document links open in the browser instead of replacing the app window
required.summary: Nothing intercepted anchor clicks, so clicking an ordinary https link in a rendered document navigated the application's own window to the remote page — a chrome-less window with no address bar and no back button, escapable only by quitting. A delegated document-level handler now routes links through a new OpenExternalURL binding, which re-checks the scheme in Go rather than trusting the webview, because the webview is where untrusted document content is parsed.

required.title: Imported image references are valid markdown and keep their alt text
required.summary: Image references were built with raw string formatting, so the default macOS screenshot name — which contains spaces — produced a destination no CommonMark parser reads as a link, and the app's own image feature wrote broken markdown into the document and saved it. Destinations are now percent-encoded and the loader decodes before every check that reads the path, so an encoded traversal cannot slip past containment. Separately, the vendored editor stores its resize ratio in the image alt attribute and discards the text on parse, so every alt became 1.00 on open; alt text is now recorded per destination in document order and restored on serialize, which also fixes captions being lost when one asset is referenced twice and when an alt is bracketed or numeric.

required.title: WYSIWYG markdown rewriting is measured and disclosed
required.summary:
The WYSIWYG surface parses markdown into the vendored editor's document model and re-serializes the whole document, so constructs the model cannot express are rewritten and an edit's blast radius is the entire file. Red-team measurement found inline
deleted outright, link reference definitions deleted and inlined, CRLF rewritten whole-file, and a range of respellings. None of it was disclosed, and the README claimed the opposite. The behaviour is now recorded in e2e/fidelity_test.go, which fails if any of it changes, and the README leads with a caution naming each case and directing users to Raw mode when exact bytes matter. This is disclosure, not repair — the defect follows from the vendored editor's model and alternative editing engines are under evaluation.

required.title: Builds report their real version instead of 1.0.0
required.summary: Every build ever produced identified itself as 1.0.0, because the darwin Info.plist hardcoded both version keys and wails.json carried no info block to override them. With no logging reaching users, the version string is the only build identity a bug report could carry, so alpha, beta and GA were indistinguishable in the field. The plist now takes the product version from wails.json so it is declared once and follows the release.

required.title: Image command fails loud instead of silently doing nothing
required.summary: The Image command inserted nothing and reported nothing when the import could not proceed, and a stale assertion still expected the removed placeholder, leaving the suite red at HEAD. Unsaved documents are now rejected before the picker opens, rejected imports leave the document unchanged, and the stale assertion was reconciled with the native import contract.

required.title: Image asset management
required.summary: Images import through the native picker or a dropped file, copy into a per-document asset folder with deterministic collision suffixes, render from inlined bytes on every surface including print/export, show a visible broken state when an asset is missing, and expose width, alt text, replace, reveal, and delete controls on the selected image block.

required.title: Corrupt preferences no longer prevent startup
required.summary: A malformed preferences.json failed Load, rejected through to a boot path with no catch, and left a blank window with no in-app recovery. Load now quarantines the bad file and returns defaults, boot catches so no bridge call can stop the editor mounting, and preferences share the document atomic write primitive so the truncation cannot be produced.

required.title: Image resolution pinned on every render surface
required.summary: resolveImageAssets had three call sites and tests pinned two; the split-preview call could be deleted with the full suite green. One fixture now asserts resolution on the formatted editor, split preview and print surfaces, so an unresolved fourth surface fails an existing test.
evidence: slop-ferret sweep @802c061 (VERIFIED by mutation on a scratch copy)

required.title: Writes never infer their target document
required.summary: Go held a single ambient (currentPath, currentText) while the frontend is multi-tab, so the quit-time close guard wrote the active tab's text to whatever file had last been opened — destroying a document the user had not touched. Reproduced. The frontend now reports every tab with its own path and dirty flag, and each dirty tab is saved to its own file.

required.title: Unsaved changes aggregate across tabs
required.summary: Dirty state tracked the active document only, so quitting with a clean tab in front discarded every edited background tab with no prompt.

required.title: Document-supplied asset paths are contained
required.summary: The product views arbitrary markdown, and every image reference resolves automatically on render. LoadForDocument honoured absolute paths, '..' traversal and any extension, so opening a document could read any file the user could read into the DOM. Documents may now only reference assets at or below their own directory, re-checked after symlink resolution.

required.title: The round-trip corpus can fail
required.summary: The corpus compared app.getMarkdown() — the cached input string — against the fixture, so it never invoked the WYSIWYG serializer and could not fail for the class of defect it existed to catch. It now reads the editor's own serialized output; demonstrated by breaking the serializer and observing the old corpus report ok while the new one failed naming the fixture.

required.title: Saving preserves symlinks and file mode
required.summary: Atomic save renamed over the target path, replacing a symlink with a regular file so the edit landed in a decoy while the real note kept its old bytes, and resetting every saved file to 0600. Writes now follow the link and keep the existing mode.

required.title: README claims corrected
required.summary: The platform badge advertised Windows and Linux for a macOS-only build, the feature list claimed build-macos.sh produces a signed .app while the script contains no codesign at all, and the round-trip corpus was described as a gate it could not be.

required.title: Continuous integration runs the gates that were hand-run
required.summary: Every gate was hand-run, and the cost was measurable: the v0.4.0 release artifact was two rounds stale and contained none of the security fixes it was meant to ship, and the architecture data drifted from the code for four commits. CI now runs gofmt, go vet, the full suite and a frontend syntax check on every push, with the e2e opt-out deliberately unset because CI is exactly where a silent skip must never apply. It found a real defect on its first run: a font test hardcoded macOS's per-user directory and had only ever passed on the author's machine.

required.title: Vendored bundles carry verified digests
required.summary: tools/vendor.sh fetches roughly 6 MB of third-party JavaScript over the network and recorded no integrity information; the Crepe bundle is patched in place after download, so the committed artifact matches no upstream artifact and its provenance could not be re-established. Digests for all 26 files are recorded and verified by a script that never touches the network. The patch step also had no else branch, so an upstream shape change would skip it silently and the editor would never mount; it now fails loudly.

required.title: Asset loading is bounded by file type as well as directory
required.summary: Containment bounded the directory but not the file type: any extension fell back to application/octet-stream and its bytes were inlined as a data URI, so .env, id_rsa and secrets.yaml beside a document were readable — and rendering resolves every image reference automatically with no user interaction. Loading now refuses anything that is not a known image type, before reading the bytes, and the importer refuses the same set so it cannot write a reference the renderer will not display.

required.title: Saving no longer clobbers a change made on disk
required.summary: Nothing compared the file on disk against what the app last saw, so a git pull, a sync client or a second window was replaced with no error and no prompt. Raised as a blocking finding in ABORT Round 1 and carried across three rounds without justification. Saving now compares against what the app last read or wrote — not what it first opened, which would make every second save look stale — and prompts on a real conflict while leaving ordinary saves uninterrupted.

required.title: Saving preserves extended attributes and refuses read-only targets
required.summary: Replacing a file by rename gives up the original inode, and extended attributes hang off the inode: a user who tagged a note in Finder lost the tag on the first save. Attributes are now carried onto the replacement, best effort so a filesystem without xattr support cannot fail a save. A read-only file was still replaced because rename needs directory permission rather than file permission; that now fails. Hard links remain broken by rename, deliberately, because the alternative is the non-atomic write the package exists to prevent.

required.title: Failures leave a trail that can be root-caused
required.summary: Nothing survived a session: frontend diagnostics were console warnings with no devtools in a production build, and Go errors surfaced only as a modal that vanished when dismissed. A reported failure could not be tied to a build or reproduced. Bounded structured records now sit beside the preference store, wired into open, save, save failure and the conflict path, with a binding so frontend diagnostics join the same trail. Recording can never fail the caller, trimming keeps the newest entries, and values are JSON-encoded so an untrusted document path cannot forge a record.

required.title:
Inline
is no longer deleted
required.summary:
The vendored editor writes
to mark an empty paragraph and strips that exact set of spellings when parsing so its own marker round-trips; genuine
was collateral, removed and joining the words either side. The match is case-sensitive, which is why
always survived — and that asymmetry proved this was never a general HTML failure, since , , , comments and block
all round-trip byte-identically. Break tags are swapped for a spelling outside the stripped set and restored in document order, using a sentinel the same length as the longest spelling it replaces so table column padding is unaffected.

required.title: CRLF line endings survive an edit
required.summary: Line endings are a property of the file, not the editing surface, and both surfaces destroyed them: the WYSIWYG editor re-serializes with LF and a textarea normalizes CRLF per the HTML spec, so a Windows-authored file came back whole-file changed after a one-word edit. Normalizing on the way in and restoring on the way out fixes both surfaces at one seam and keeps dirty tracking in a single representation.

workstreams.name: Editor shell
workstreams.summary: Turn the concept shell screens into backed macOS editor functionality without rendering fake controls.
evidence: Non-tool Go coverage: 80.5% statements after native App seam and preference-store tests.

blockers.title: GA shipped over a NO-GO ABORT verdict, with disclosure as the mitigation
blockers.summary:
The 2026-08-08 ABORT review returned NO-GO from all five red-team stations over four rounds. The maintainer accepted the residual risk and authorised the 0.4.0 GA release on 2026-08-08. The mitigation is disclosure, not repair: the README now leads with a caution that WYSIWYG editing rewrites markdown the vendored editor cannot represent — deleting inline
and link reference definitions, rewriting CRLF, and changing lines the user never touched — and directs users to Raw mode when exact bytes matter. Recorded as ACCEPTED rather than resolved, because the underlying fidelity defect is open: it follows from the vendored editor's parse-and-re-serialize model and cannot be patched at the seams. Alternative editing engines are under evaluation. Full record: docs/releases/v0.4.0-abort.md.

evidence.label: slop-ferret sweep @802c061 (tier 1-2, 2 VERIFIED blocking, both fixed)
